quote: Beweise dass es keine andere Zahl im Kreis- körper giebt ausser der Einheitswurzel selbst deren Diskriminante gleich der Diskriminan- te des Körpers ist.
english: Prove that there is no number in the cyclotomic field other than the root of unity itself whose discriminant equals the discriminant of the field.
topic: Three short notes: Minkowski's conjecture that a closed surface of flexible but inextensible material cannot be continuously bent (especially the sphere); whether all ruler-and-compass constructions can be done with compass alone; and a task to prove that no number in the cyclotomic field other than the root of unity has discriminant equal to the field discriminant.

triage.modern_statement: Let K = Q(ζ_n) be a cyclotomic field. Its ring of integers is O_K = Z[ζ_n]. In modern terms the question asks which α ∈ O_K satisfy disc(α) = d_K, i.e. Z[α] = O_K, so that α generates a power integral basis (K is 'monogenic' via α). Hilbert's claim is that ζ (with the trivially equivalent elements ±ζ^k + integer translates and Galois conjugates) gives the only such generators. As literally stated, the claim is false: α = 1/(1+ζ) and its equivalents also give Z[α] = O_K. The corrected modern form is Bremner's 1988 conjecture: up to the equivalences α ↦ ±α + c (c ∈ Z) and conjugation, the only generators of power integral bases of Q(ζ_p) are ζ and 1/(1+ζ). Gaál–Robertson (2006) proved the analogous statement for prime-power cyclotomic fields under a class-number condition.
triage.answered_by: This was not settled in Hilbert's form, and that form turned out to be false. A. Bremner (J. Number Theory 28, 1988, 288–298) observed that there are further 'non-obvious' generators such as 1/(1+ζ). He conjectured that, up to equivalence, there are no others and proved this for p=7. A source summary credits Nagell with earlier work on p=5. L. Robertson (J. Number Theory 1998, 'Power bases for cyclotomic integer rings') gave a method for checking the conjecture prime by prime. Robertson (J. Number Theory 88, 2001) settled the 2-power cyclotomic fields. Gaál & Robertson (J. Number Theory 120, 2006) handled odd prime powers p^m under the condition gcd(h_q^+, p(p−1)/2) = 1. Robertson ('Monogeneity in cyclotomic fields', IJNT 7(7), 2011) found all power integral bases for n = 15, 20, 21, 28 and proposed a conjectural general answer. I found no source showing that the unconditional general case has been proved.

evidence.claim: Bremner (1988) studied power bases in Q(ζ_p). He noted that besides ζ there are 'non-obvious' generators of Z[ζ], conjectured that up to conjugacy there are no others, and proved this for Q(ζ_7).
Robertson (1998): for an odd prime p, O_p = Z[α] if α = ζ or 1/(1+ζ) (or equivalents). The paper cites Bremner's 1988 conjecture that up to integer translation there are no further generators.
Robertson determined all power integral bases in 2-power cyclotomic fields (J. Number Theory 88, 2001, 196–209).
Gaál and Robertson (J. Number Theory 120, 2006) treat prime-power cyclotomic fields Q(ζ_{p^m}) under the condition gcd(h_q^+, p(p−1)/2) = 1.

Robertson's 'Monogeneity in cyclotomic fields' (IJNT 2011) finds all power integral bases for n = 15, 20, 21, 28 and gives a conjectural solution to finding all integral generators of cyclotomic fields.
A survey notes Bremner's conjecture for primes p > 3 and that Robertson found a way to check it for primes up to a bound.

triage.why: Hilbert's note asks for all α in a cyclotomic field with disc(α) = disc(K). This is the problem of finding all generators of power integral bases (monogenity) of cyclotomic fields. Bremner (1988) showed that Hilbert's conjectured answer, ζ only, is wrong because 1/(1+ζ) also works. The corrected statement, Bremner's conjecture, has been proved for p=7, for 2-power fields, for prime powers under a class-number condition, and for some small composite n. The sources I found indicate that the general case remains a conjecture, studied in the ongoing research area of monogenity and power integral bases (Gaál, Robertson and others). It is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem. I found no source linking Hilbert's diary note to this literature. My confidence is medium because I could not confirm the current status of the general conjecture from recent sources.
